sections.title: The letter i
paragraphs: The letter (i) /i/ makes three related sounds. Its main sound is heard in the word (isla) /ˈiz.la/, which means island. A vowel is a sound made with open air and no touch in the mouth. This vowel stays very crisp and clear every time you say it.

sections.title: Saying the sounds
paragraphs: For the main sound, push your tongue forward and high near the roof of your mouth. Spread your lips wide like a smile and let your voice ring out. For the other two sounds, move your tongue even closer to the roof of your mouth. Air glides quickly into or out of the next vowel without stopping. Touch your throat to feel your voice shake.

sections.title: Reading the letter
paragraphs: As a syllable centre, this letter makes its clear sound in (mío) /ˈmi.o/. Before another vowel in the same beat, it acts like a quick glide in (bien) /bjen/. When it stands after another vowel in the same beat, it finishes the glide smoothly in (aire) /ˈai̯.ɾe/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not turn this vowel into the relaxed sound of bit. Keep your tongue very high and tight, as in machine. Do not stretch it into a long glide like sea. Spanish vowels remain steady, crisp and short from start to finish.
